summary: The selected papers emphasize cross-system tests of jet energy loss, robust noncritical baselines for high-baryon-density cumulants, late-stage effects in open charm, and experimentally grounded ML for detector reconstruction. The strongest heavy-ion contribution applies a common DREENA setup from O+O to Pb+Pb; the strongest ML contribution validates transformer-based AC-LGAD position reconstruction on SPS test-beam data.
professional_summary: System-size jet-quenching tests, cumulant-background control, open-charm hadronic rescattering, multi-strange recombination, AC-LGAD waveform reconstruction, and domain adaptation are the central themes.
strongest_paper: arXiv:2611.12404 — common-parameter O-to-Pb high-pT phenomenology with falsifiable harmonic, fluctuation, and flavor predictions.
strongest_paper_summary: Common-parameter O-to-Pb high-pT phenomenology supplies the day's most direct heavy-ion tests; real test-beam validation makes the AC-LGAD transformer the strongest ML result.

papers.title: From oxygen to lead: testing a common QGP description with high-pT probes
papers.short_authors: Bithika Karmakar, Dusan Zigic, Magdalena Djordjevic
papers.abstract: The observation of suppression and finite high-pT elliptic anisotropy in O+O and Ne+Ne raises the question of whether a common QGP description can simultaneously account for both observables across systems from oxygen to lead. The authors couple event-by-event bulk evolution constrained by soft observables to DREENA radiative and collisional energy loss, using the same microscopic parameter set for O+O, Ne+Ne, Xe+Xe, and Pb+Pb. They reproduce the ordering of suppression and predict system-, harmonic-, fluctuation-, and flavor-dependent tests.
papers.summary: Uses one microscopic energy-loss parameter set across O+O, Ne+Ne, Xe+Xe, and Pb+Pb and turns the common-QGP hypothesis into a suite of falsifiable high-pT predictions, including v2/(1-RAA), v3, cumulant ratios, and D/B mesons.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong phenomenology with a coherent cross-system design and concrete predictions. The present evidence is still model-conditional: agreement with the ordering of suppression does not uniquely validate DREENA, and several headline observables await measurement.

papers.title: Proton Number Fluctuations in Au+Au and Ag+Ag Collisions at sqrt(sNN)=2.4 GeV: A JAM Model Study
papers.short_authors: Yongcong Xu, Zhaohui Wang, Yu Zhang, Xiaofeng Luo
papers.abstract: Proton-number cumulants and factorial cumulants through fourth order are studied in Au+Au and Ag+Ag collisions at 2.4 GeV using JAM in cascade and mean-field modes. The CIGAR procedure closely reproduces a participant-number reference and outperforms multiplicity-based centrality treatment; mean fields, rapidity acceptance, and a simplified light-nucleus removal prescription materially affect cumulant ratios.
papers.summary: Builds a noncritical hadronic-transport baseline for high-baryon-density fluctuation measurements and explicitly tests centrality, acceptance, mean-field, and light-nucleus effects.
papers.critical_assessment: Methodologically strong because CIGAR is checked against a participant-number reference and several confounders are separated. The light-nucleus treatment is intentionally schematic and the result remains a JAM-dependent baseline, not a quantitative uncertainty envelope.

papers.title: Hadronic final-state effects on open-charm production at LHC energies
papers.short_authors: Taesoo Song, Elena Bratkovskaya, Krzysztof Redlich
papers.abstract: PHSD calculations with and without charm-hadron rescattering are compared with ALICE measurements and statistical-hadronization expectations. Integrated relative D-meson yields are largely insensitive to hadronic interactions, while low- and intermediate-pT spectra and elliptic flow are modified; the model also reproduces the system trend of Ds+/D0.
papers.summary: Separates open-charm observables that are robust against the hadronic stage from those that receive material late-stage modifications.
papers.critical_assessment: A useful controlled switch-off study tied to ALICE data and an established transport framework. Its reach is limited by the short paper, one transport implementation, and the absence of a broad parameter or model uncertainty analysis.

papers.title: Elliptic flow of phi and Omega via quark recombination mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: A quark-recombination model with strange-quark phase space parameterized by a viscous blast wave describes phi and Omega elliptic flow from 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV. The analysis finds approximate constituent-quark scaling, but at LHC energies the extracted strange-quark v2 differs appreciably from naively scaled hadron v2.
papers.summary: Tests recombination and NCQ scaling for multi-strange hadrons over an unusually broad energy range and highlights where interpreting scaled hadron flow as partonic flow fails.
papers.critical_assessment: Interesting and potentially useful, but the broad claim of recombination validity rests on a parameterized blast-wave input and a narrow observable set. Agreement with v2 alone does not uniquely establish constituent-quark degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Test beam results for machine-learning-based reconstruction of resistive silicon sensors
papers.short_authors: Don C. Wong, Leena Diehl, Spencer Ellis, et al.
papers.abstract: A topology-agnostic transformer reconstructs positions from full AC-LGAD waveforms measured in a 120 GeV pion test beam and is compared with a parameter-free charge-imbalance estimator and fitted matrix inversion. With an in-situ-calibrated 2.5 micrometer telescope pointing resolution, the transformer improves median position error by up to a factor of three over the full active pad; all methods converge in the charge-sharing core.
papers.summary: Validates learned waveform reconstruction on a real SPS beam with calibrated telescope resolution and meaningful analytic baselines.
papers.critical_assessment: The strongest ML paper in this batch because evaluation uses real beam data, calibrated reference tracking, and analytic baselines. The gain is spatially nonuniform, and generalization beyond one 2x2-pad device and its operating conditions remains untested.

papers.title: Domain Adaptive Graph Neural Networks for Neutrino Experiments
papers.short_authors: Hemalata Nayak, Giuseppe Cerati, Aleksandra Ciprijanovic, Tammy Walton
papers.abstract: Adversarial domain adaptation is added to GNN reconstruction trained on the MicroBooNE open dataset. Four unlabeled target domains are synthesized using scale, noise, and position-dependent signal perturbations. Target-domain precision improves by as much as 0.19 and recall by 0.37 without a substantial source-domain penalty.
papers.summary: Targets the simulation-to-data mismatch in LArTPC reconstruction using adversarial domain adaptation and reports substantial recovery under four controlled shifts.
papers.critical_assessment: Promising and correctly focused on robustness, but the target domains are engineered perturbations rather than real detector data. Results are workshop-level evidence of stress-test recovery, not yet proof of simulation-to-data closure.

cautions.title: Machine learning assisted neutrino/antineutrino discrimination in atmospheric neutrino events for CPV sensitivity in a 20-kton liquid scintillator detector
cautions.short_authors: Dek Hao Liew, Mohammad Nizam, Shu Tian Eu, Siew Yan Hoh
cautions.abstract: GENIE events in a JUNO-like geometry are passed through parameterized smearing, and logistic regression, XGBoost, and an MLP use inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and lepton energy for statistical neutrino/antineutrino separation. XGBoost reaches AUC near 0.83 and improves an approximate peak CP-violation sensitivity, with nuisance parameters marginalized.
cautions.summary: The proposed statistical separation is plausible, but the claimed sensitivity gain is obtained with a simplified detector response.
cautions.critical_assessment: The authors appropriately call the results preliminary. Until neutron response, event reconstruction, backgrounds, and correlated detector/systematic uncertainties are validated in a full simulation, the quoted significance gains should not be treated as an experimental projection.

cautions.title: Critical Temperature in Nonextensive Hadron Models: A Pressure-based Approach
cautions.short_authors: M. A. A. Ahmed, H. Zainuddin
cautions.abstract: A pressure equation derived from Tsallis entropy is explored for several bag-model variants. The inferred transition temperatures depend strongly on the nonextensive parameter and model term, with quoted values well below the modern lattice-QCD crossover scale for physical quark masses; multiple mathematical roots can appear at finite volume.
cautions.summary: The mathematical root structure is clear, but its connection to the QCD crossover in heavy-ion matter is not adequately established.
cautions.critical_assessment: The paper combines phenomenological nonextensivity and model-dependent bag terms without a convincing calibration to lattice thermodynamics or a controlled uncertainty analysis. Calling the resulting weighted value a critical temperature risks giving model algebra more physical authority than the validation supports.
